prospects.thesis: Booz Allen sits at the intersection of defense IT modernization and AI deployment for federal agencies, giving it exposure to two of the strongest secular tailwinds. At just 0.7x P/S with a $8.2B market cap, it offers rare value in a sector where multiples have expanded sharply, and the +11.9% 1M move signals institutional accumulation ahead of continued DoD AI/cyber contract flow. Bullish options and institutional signals confirm the setup.

UiPath is the pure-play RPA leader pivoting into agentic AI automation, a category gaining enterprise traction as CIOs rationalize AI spend toward measurable ROI use cases. The +16% 1M move with bullish options flow and institutional accumulation suggests smart money is positioning ahead of a fundamental inflection, and at 3.9x P/S with a $6.5B cap it remains reasonably priced versus AI peers. Small-cap AI exposure diversifies the watchlist away from mega-cap concentration.

HII is the sole builder of U.S. nuclear-powered aircraft carriers and one of only two submarine builders, giving it an irreplaceable moat as naval shipbuilding budgets accelerate under AUKUS and Pacific deterrence priorities. At 0.9x P/S and $12.4B cap, it's structurally cheap while +12.6% 1M momentum reflects visibility into multi-decade backlog. Differentiates from BAH (services) by adding hard-asset naval exposure.

SMCI is the leading builder of GPU-optimized AI server systems, directly leveraged to hyperscaler and enterprise AI capex cycles. The -5.3% 1M dip against a strong tape offers a rare entry point in a name where P/S is only 0.5x, and bullish options positioning suggests traders are anticipating a rebound tied to next-gen Blackwell platform ramps. The prior accounting overhang has largely cleared, but caution warrants a "Watch" rating pending confirmation of stabilization.

GitLab's Duo AI coding assistant and full DevSecOps platform position it as a beneficiary of enterprise consolidation of developer tooling and AI-driven code generation adoption. At 5.7x P/S with a $5.7B cap and +11% 1M momentum plus bullish institutional positioning, it offers a differentiated AI-software angle distinct from PATH's automation focus. Near-term catalyst is continued Duo attach-rate expansion driving net revenue retention re-acceleration.

market_pulse.rotation_analysis: Big money is piling into Energy, Real Estate, and Consumer Discretionary — that Energy bid lines up with the administration's "drill baby drill" posture, permitting rollbacks, and the ongoing SPR refill talk, while Real Estate is quietly getting bought as traders sniff out that the Fed's next move is more likely a cut than a hike, which would juice REITs that have been crushed by high rates. The Consumer Discretionary call-buying is the spiciest signal — someone's betting the tariff drama gets resolved or that consumers keep spending through it, possibly front-running holiday season strength or tax-cut extension chatter out of the Hill. On the flip side, the smart money is aggressively hedging Tech, Communications, Healthcare, and Industrials — Tech and Comms are getting antitrust and AI-regulation shadows plus stretched valuations, Healthcare is bracing for drug-pricing executive orders and Medicare negotiation expansion, and Industrials are exposed if tariffs bite global supply chains harder than expected. The truly weird tell is the massive put buying in Utilities and Staples — those are supposed to be safe havens, so when people are paying up to hedge the defensives *too*, it usually means they're not preparing for a normal rotation but for a broad de-risking event, and the widening credit spreads with bearish HYG/LQD flow confirms that fear is leaking into the bond market.
